# TurboPDF

> HTML, React, Markdown or a JSON document tree → PDF, with a native Rust engine. No browser, no network,
> no scripts. Node.js ≥ 20, TypeScript types included. Package: `turbopdf`.

This file is for AI coding assistants. It is the whole API in one page. Full guide: docs/guide.md.

## Rules that are easy to get wrong

- `turbopdf.create(string)` treats the string as **HTML**. Markdown always goes through `{ markdown }`.
- Pass exactly one source: `html`, `react`, `markdown` or `tree`.
- Nothing is fetched over the network. Remote images, stylesheets and fonts are skipped with a warning.
  Download them yourself, or pass `data:` URLs or local paths.
- Relative paths are read from `baseDir` (default: the working directory) and never outside it.
- JavaScript in the HTML never runs. Render data into the markup first, or use React.
- Component and tree sizes are in points (1/72 in). CSS lengths are CSS (`px`, `mm`, `em`…).
- Unsupported: WOFF/WOFF2 and web fonts loaded from a URL (use local TTF/OTF files). `float` works for simple cases (columns, a logo or image with text beside it); prefer Flexbox or Grid for layouts.
- Edge runtimes / browsers: `import { init, create } from 'turbopdf/edge'`, `await init(wasm)` once (wasm = `turbopdf/turbopdf.wasm`, its bytes or a URL), then `create()` (React: `init(wasm, { renderToStaticMarkup })` from `react-dom/server`); output with `toUint8Array()` / `toResponse()` (no `save`, no files: fonts as bytes, images as data: URLs).
- Problems are **returned** in `pdf.warnings`, not thrown. Check them, or pass `strict: true` to throw.

## Create

```ts
import turbopdf, { TurboPdfError } from 'turbopdf';

const pdf = await turbopdf.create('<h1>Invoice</h1>');                    // HTML
await turbopdf.create({ html, css: 'h1{color:#1d4ed8}', baseDir: './templates' });
await turbopdf.create(<Invoice id={42} />);                                // React element
await turbopdf.create({ markdown: '# Report\n\n| a | b |\n|---|---|\n| 1 | 2 |' });
await turbopdf.create({ tree });                                            // JSON tree, types in 'turbopdf/tree'
```

Options (every source): `format` ('A3' | 'A4' | 'A5' | 'Letter' | 'Legal', default A4), `orientation`
('portrait' | 'landscape'), `width`/`height` (custom size), `margin` ('10mm' default; a CSS length, a number of CSS pixels, or { top, right, bottom, left }),
`css`, `header`/`footer` (HTML, `{page}` and `{pages}` are replaced), `fonts` ([{ family, path | data, weight?, style? }]),
`watermark` ('PAID' or { text, color, fontSize, fontWeight, angle }), `title`, `lang`, `bookmarks` (true),
`tagged` (true), `pdfua` (false; needs title and lang), `timeout` (30000 ms), `strict` (false), `signal`, `baseDir`.

## Output

```ts
await pdf.save('out/invoice.pdf');
pdf.toBuffer();                                            // Buffer
pdf.toStream();                                            // Node stream (Express: pdf.toStream().pipe(res))
pdf.toResponse({ filename: 'invoice.pdf', disposition: 'attachment' });   // web Response (Next.js, Hono, Bun, Deno)
pdf.pages;                                                 // page count
pdf.warnings;                                              // { type, message, path?, page? }[]
const preview = await pdf.preview();                       // HTML/CSS: { style, pages: [{ page, width, height, html }], toHtml() }
const pngs = await pdf.toPng({ scale: 2 });                // [{ page, save(path), toDataUrl() }]
```

## Components (`turbopdf/components`)

`Document` (title, author, lang, pdfua…), `Page` (size, orientation, margin, header, footer, watermark), `View` (flexbox,
column by default; link, keepTogether, role), `Text`, `Span`, `Link` (href: URL or `#id`), `Heading` (level 1–6),
`Image` (src: path, data URL or bytes; fit, alt), `QR` (value, size, ecc, color, background), `Table` (columns,
repeatHeader, headerStyle, cellStyle, altRowStyle) / `Row` (header) / `Cell` (colSpan), `PageNumber` (format
'{page}/{pages}', target), `PageBreak`, `TableOfContents`, `KeepTogether`, `Spacer`, `Divider`.

```tsx
<Document title="Invoice 42" lang="en">
  <Page margin={36} footer={<PageNumber format="Page {page} / {pages}" />}>
    <Heading>Invoice 42</Heading>
    <Table columns={[{ width: 'auto' }, { width: 80, align: 'right' }]}>
      <Row header><Cell><Text>Item</Text></Cell><Cell><Text>Price</Text></Cell></Row>
      <Row><Cell><Text>Logo</Text></Cell><Cell><Text>450 €</Text></Cell></Row>
    </Table>
    <QR value="https://acme.com/pay/42" size={72} alt="Pay online" />
  </Page>
</Document>
```

## Document tree (JSON, the format an LLM can emit directly)

```json
{ "type": "document", "version": 1, "meta": { "title": "Hello", "lang": "en" },
  "children": [{ "type": "page", "children": [
    { "type": "heading", "level": 1, "content": "Hello" },
    { "type": "text", "content": "Generated by a model." },
    { "type": "image", "src": { "qr": "https://acme.com" }, "style": { "width": 72, "height": 72 } }
  ]}] }
```

Node types: `view`, `text`, `heading`, `image`, `table`, `page_break`, `page_number`, `table_of_contents`. When the tree is invalid,
`create` throws a `TurboPdfError` with `code: 'invalid_tree'`:

- If the JSON has the wrong shape (a missing field, an unknown type), the `message` gives the line and column.
- If the values are wrong (heading level 9, empty QR…), `details` is `[{ path, code, message }]`, one entry per problem.

## HTML and CSS that work

Selectors: type, class, id, attribute, descendant, `>`, `:first-child`, `:last-child`, `:nth-child()`, `::before`/`::after`.
Properties: `display` block/flex/grid/none, Flexbox, Grid (`fr`, `repeat()`), width/height (min/max), margin, padding, border,
border-radius, background(-color), color, font-*, line-height, text-align, `position: absolute`, `break-before/after/inside`,
`calc()`, `var()`, `@page { size; margin }`, `@media print`, local `@font-face`. Elements: block elements, p, h1–h6, span, b, i,
br, hr, `a href`, `img` (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, SVG), inline `<svg>`, table/thead (header repeats on every page), ul/ol, pre, blockquote.
QR codes: `<img src="qr:TEXT" width="90">`, or `![alt](qr:TEXT)` in Markdown.
Page-break classes: `turbopdf-break-before`, `turbopdf-break-after`, `turbopdf-keep-together`.
Markdown extras: `<!-- pagebreak -->` and `<!-- toc -->`.

## Warnings (`pdf.warnings[].type`)

`overflow`, `moved_to_next_page`, `missing_glyph`, `image_failed`, `stylesheet_failed`, `font_failed`, `broken_link`,
`missing_alt`. Each `message` says how to fix the problem. Feed the messages back to the model and render again.

## Errors (`TurboPdfError.code`)

`invalid_source`, `render_timeout`, `render_failed`, `invalid_tree`, `font_failed`, `not_accessible`, `engine_unavailable`,
`react_not_installed`, `warnings_found` (strict), `aborted`.
